_readme: Source of truth for wordshaping.org. Every word carries 'proposed' — the form exactly as first written by its author, which is displayed on the word's page as a first-class field, never as an erratum. Add sightings to the 'sightings' array, then run python3 build.py. Sightings are the only thing the leaderboard ranks; 'score' is one reader's opinion and sorts nothing.

words.def: Publishing something extravagant while affixing a disclaimer that absolves nothing and advertises everything. Of an object: bearing a disclaimer as composition rather than appendix — the hedge given margin, weight and iconography.
words.cite: He posted this image disclaimerciously.
words.etym: disclaimer + -ciously, on the model of capriciously, speciously, graciously. An ear-word, not a rule-word: -cious is inherited and needs a -ce stem, so this works by echo rather than by rule.
words.note: The buried mercy was never designed in. A disclaimer is a plea for clemency entered in advance, and the word admits it under its breath. Stress travels exactly one syllable — the rule that later decided six other words in this collection.

words.def: Subscription sustained without attention; the dutiful maintenance of a following one does not read.
words.cite: Her feed was mostly followance.
words.etym: follow + -ance, licensed outright by allowance — the identical -ow + -ance junction, no stress shift.
words.note: On the model of attendance (presence without engagement) and observance (practice without belief). Following names the act or the crowd; followership names the role. Neither names the condition.

words.def: Possibility held as identity. Faces forward — the novel always going to be written, the potential one is perpetually sitting on.
words.cite: It was couldism all the way down, and a very good CV.
words.etym: could + -ism, on the model of whataboutism, where -ism attaches to a conversational move rather than a doctrine.
words.note: Could is a past tense doing non-past work, because English marks unreality as pastness. The base carries 'not real' before the suffix adds anything. Third member of the set is taken: Karen Horney named the tyranny of the should in 1950.

words.def: The counterfactual held as identity. Faces back — I would have been a—
words.cite: Every family dinner ended in wouldism.
words.etym: would + -ism. Pairs with couldism: same distance from the real, opposite directions.
words.note: Deployed in the wild before it was formally used — 'hackification could have occurred' is a couldism aimed at a real event.

words.def: The process by which art becomes gentrified enough to be categorised into genres.
words.cite: The scene survived everything except genrification.
words.etym: genre + -ification, blended with gentrification. The parents are one phoneme apart — gen-TRI- against gen-RI- — which is as close as a portmanteau can get.
words.note: The parents are cognates. Genre is Latin genus (kind); gentrification runs back through gentry, gentle, gentilis to gens (clan). Both from PIE *gen-, to beget. The blend reunites words that were one word before Latin. Pronunciation must choose a parent: /dʒ/ makes the gentrification echo audible, /ʒ/ keeps the genre root.

sightings.what: Word set as a dictionary definition with IPA, circulated as an image.

words.def: The restructuring of a rule system around its exceptions, continued until the exceptions constitute the system.
words.cite: Procurement reform ended in quiet loopholification.
words.etym: loophole + -ification. Noun base, so the suffix has work to do.
words.note: The only -ification here with no plain nominalisation squatting on it. Forms: loopholify (v.), loopholous (adj.), loopholously (adv.).

words.def: Work restructured around the measurement of winning, until the measuring is the work.
words.cite: Two quarters of successification and nobody could say what shipped.
words.etym: success + -ification. Success is a noun, -ify takes nouns, no squatter holds the slot. The chain runs exactly like class → classify → classification.
words.note: The cleanest -ification in the collection by formation.

words.def: Generative decay; breakdown that is the point. The dead thing becoming the material of the next thing.
words.cite: Two years of compostification, and the failed company had fed four better ones.
words.etym: compost + -ification. Compost is Latinate — from compositum, 'something put together' — so the Latin suffix is coming home rather than crashing a Germanic party. Same root as composite, compound, composition, compote.
words.note: The only honest agent-deletion in the collection. Every other -ification here hides a hand that really exists; nothing decomposes a compost pile. The agentless suffix finally describes an agentless process.

words.def: The conversion of ordinary objects into attack surface — fridges, doorbells, pacemakers, thermostats.
words.cite: Hackification could have occurred.
words.etym: hack + -ification. Noun base, clean chain, no squatter: hacking has a hacker in it, this has none.
words.note: Deployed with 'could have occurred', which is breach-notification English — no actor, no certainty. Both halves delete the responsible party: the noun removes the hacker, the modal removes the event.

sightings.what: Title card reading 'hackification could have occurred'.

words.def: The mechanism rather than the state — the incremental path by which individually reasonable decisions arrive at disaster with nobody having chosen it.
words.cite: Six months of clusterfuckification, and not one meeting where anyone decided anything wrong.
words.etym: clusterfuck + -ification. Noun base. The suffixes want opposite bases: -ation takes verbs, -ify takes nouns.
words.note: The register clash is an asset, unlike followification: chaos described in the language of process is the joke and the meaning. Squatter warning — clusterfuckery is probably already in the wild.

words.def: The process by which a domain becomes source material — the point at which nothing is made, only recombined.
words.cite: Fifty-eight turns of remixifying English morphemes.
words.etym: remix + -ification. Noun base; mix is Latinate (miscere), so the register sits comfortably.
words.note: Lessig's remix culture names the condition; this names the process. Agentless in the useful way — remixing has a remixer in it, this does not.

words.def: The conversion of every relation — colleagues, clergy, physicians, friends — into an account one subscribes to asymmetrically.
words.cite: The followification of the newsroom.
words.etym: follow (n.) + -ification.
words.note: -ify resists plain Germanic stems, and where it takes them the result is comic — speechify, citify, argufy. Lands as satire whether or not satire was intended. The process; followance is what it leaves behind.

words.def: Entanglement pursued as policy — things bound together so they cannot later be separated. Vendor lock-in, forced bundling, the merger structured to be unwindable.
words.cite: The contract was less a partnership than an intertwinification.
words.etym: intertwine + -ification. Intertwine is already a verb, so -ify is a round trip, and intertwinement holds the plain slot.
words.note: Earns the suffix only on the systemic reading, as gamification means more than 'making a game'.

words.def: The doctrine that any settled thing — a habit, a belief, an institution, a culture — is a codebase awaiting a patch.
words.cite: Every self-help shelf in the airport preaches reprogramification.
words.etym: reprogram + -ification. Reprogram is already a verb and reprogramming holds the plain nominalisation.
words.note: For an ordinary mind ordinarily being rewired, use reprogramming. This earns its keep only on the doctrinal reading.

words.def: The condition of an institution in which every process exists to prevent rather than to do; the risk register eating the whole job.
words.cite: Three years of preventification and the department had prevented everything, including itself.
words.etym: prevent + -ification.
words.note: Prevention is not boring, it is invisible — successful prevention leaves no evidence. Public health calls the adjacent problem the prevention paradox.

words.def: The reframing of a non-war thing as war — a trial, a policy dispute, a newsroom argument.
words.cite: Warification deployed by a defendant against the court trying him.
words.etym: war + -ification. Noun base, diagnostic passes cleanly.
words.note: Agentless in the honest way compostification is: nobody warifies a dispute, it becomes war-framed.

words.def: Out of a temperament organised around what one is avoiding — as distinct from preventively, which describes a purpose rather than a disposition.
words.cite: He lived preventfully, and had nothing to show for it but the absence of disasters.
words.etym: prevent + -ful + -ly. -ful takes verbs where it means 'inclined to' — forgetful, watchful, resentful, regretful.
words.note: Proposed as preventifully; the -i- was spurious. -ifully is a -y noun + -ful + -ly, and that i is a mutated y (beauty, duty, mercy). Your word minus one letter.

words.def: Polishing the wording while the substance sits untouched.
words.cite: They spent the meeting wordsmithingly, and the problem was exactly where they left it.
words.etym: wordsmith + -ingly. Clears the manner gate: wordsmithing is something a person does in a moment, with an attitude.
words.note: Proves that compounds buy syllables — WORD-smith-ing-ly survives four syllables because secondary stress on smith prevents the three-weak lapse that kills victoriful.

words.def: Building by asks given as moods rather than specifications. The input end of the thing vibe coding names at the output end.
words.cite: He created new software vibepromptingly, then read every line of it.
words.etym: vibeprompt + -ingly.
words.note: Draws a distinction nobody had. Vibe coding means accepting the output unread; this names giving the input unspecified. They come apart cleanly, which is the proof the distinction is real.

words.def: Mindfuck-adjacent. Near it, not it — pleasant weirdness rather than vertigo, with the dosage stated honestly on the label.
words.cite: Pink llamas and a yellow submarine are not a mindfuck. They are mindfuckish.
words.etym: mindfuck + -ish, one of the most productive suffixes English has left (childish, bookish, feverish, sheepish).
words.note: The only suffix in this collection whose contribution is subtraction. -ish removes confidence, and most coinages overclaim. Adverb: mindfuckishly.

words.def: Entry legitimised by an invitation the enterer arranged.
words.cite: Invited intervention: the government that requests the troops already at the border.
words.etym: invitation + invasion, blended. Both parents share two seams — the in- prefix and the -ion ending — where most blends overlap at one.
words.note: The parents are semantically adjacent: both carry Latin in-, 'into'. Invitation is calling someone in; invasion is going in uninvited. Same act, opposite permission, and the word sits on the hinge. Variant invitasion keeps both parents more audible at one syllable more.

words.def: Of an atmosphere: consumed with appetite rather than merely present. Vibey describes a room; vibelicious describes wanting to eat it.
words.cite: The whole place was vibelicious and cost nothing.
words.etym: vibe + -licious, a genuine libfix — there is no morpheme -licious, since delicious is Latin deliciosus. Speakers mis-heard the seam, extracted the fragment, and it became real.
words.note: Satisfies every -licious constraint the project found: short base, outside the suffix's home field, neutral base letting the suffix do the judging. The only one of five attempts that does.

words.def: Relishing the spectacle of an accused inverting the frame on the tribunal.
words.cite: When an alleged war criminal accuses the court of waging war.
words.etym: war criminal + -licious.
words.note: Ruled out here as a semantic mismatch — -licious encodes appetite, not inversion — and then overturned by the artifact. Deployed as pop-art, the register is appetite, and the piece relishes the reversal. The objection held only for a register it was not written in.

sightings.what: Title treatment reading 'WARCRIMINALICIOUS WAGEWARIFICATION', with strapline and disclaimer panel.

words.def: With the relish of a hacker — the pleasure of the elegant kludge. Doing it the clever way because the clever way is delicious, not because it is better.
words.cite: He solved it hackiciously, in four lines nobody else could read.
words.etym: hack + -iciously. Proposed as hackisiously; English writes /ʃəs/ as -cious, -tious or -xious, never -sious.
words.note: Monosyllabic bases cannot fail the stress test — there is nowhere for the stress to sit but adjacent to the suffix. Hackish exists (Jargon File) but only classifies; -icious evaluates.

words.def: In a manner that performs legitimacy rather than possessing it.
words.cite: The paperwork was filed legiticiously, by an office that had existed for six days.
words.etym: legit + -iciously. Proposed as legitimateciously, where the stress had to hop two syllables and could not.
words.note: Clip the base to fix the meter — le·git·I·cious·ly scans w·w·S·w·w, the identical shape as dis·clai·MER·cious·ly. The informal register does independent work: a word about performed legitimacy should not sound respectable.

words.def: By a discrete lapse in an otherwise attentive mind — as distinct from absentmindedly, which names an ongoing state.
words.cite: She addressed it brainfartingly to the whole company, having been careful all week.
words.etym: brain fart + -ingly. Proposed as brainfarticiously, where the stress had to hop two syllables from the front-stressed compound.
words.note: Fourth word built on the compound + -ingly shape, which has never once needed a correction.

words.def: Pleasingly amorphous. Referent still open — the form is sound and the meaning is unclaimed.
words.etym: blob + -licious, with an epenthetic -i- breaking the bl-/bl- cluster collision in *bloblicious.
words.note: The first justified inserted vowel in the collection. Every earlier one had no source and no motivation; this one has a job.

words.def: The absurd performed as a genre rather than arrived at.
words.etym: absurd + -alistic. The -al has no source — in natural, ideal, material, journal it belongs to the base, and there is no *absurdal.
words.note: Kept for the phantom syllable, which enacts the pomposity it names. Absurdist already exists and is already the adjective.

words.def: Listening in such a way that the seams fall somewhere other than where the history put them.
words.cite: She heard the word rebracketingly, and a new suffix fell out.
words.etym: rebracket + -ingly.
words.note: The collection's self-description: a lexicon built almost entirely by hearing seams in the wrong places, holding a word for doing exactly that. There is a racket inside rebracketingly, and finding it is itself a rebracketing.

words.def: In the manner of meaning asserted by accumulation — on the theory that enough stacked components must add up to profundity.
words.etym: A compound, not a derivation. Five elements, past the three English readers chunk comfortably.
words.note: Self-demonstrating, as sesquipedalian is a long word for long words. The lowest-scoring word here on form and the only one that enacts what it describes — which is a different axis the rubric does not have.

words.def: The removal of an occurred event from the record; an incident officially declared not to have taken place while the people who lived it remain.
words.cite: The incident was resolved by unhappening.
words.etym: un- + happen + -ing, plain reversal as in undo, untie, unsay.
words.note: Pairs with the unhappened — harm that never occurred because someone prevented it. The inflection carries the distinction: -ed never was, -ing was and then was not. Prior art nearby: memory-holing, unpersoning, retcon. This is the administrative case — the record amended, the bodies unamended.

words.def: Evidentiary appearance in excess of evidentiary content. The bar chart without an axis; the arrow diagram asserting a causation nobody measured.
words.cite: The deck scored high on infographicity and reported no findings.
words.etym: infographic + -icity, on specificity, authenticity, historicity.
words.note: Provenance: proposed as infographicously. The suffix was blocked on rule, but the replacement changed suffix, part of speech and meaning — the last supplied rather than asked for. The only entry here not descended from the word that prompted it. Prior art: Tufte's chartjunk and data-ink ratio both concern ornament on a graphic genuinely conveying data; this is the rhetorical case.

words.def: In a manner that performs success; the win assembled after the fact, the metric chosen once the number was known.
words.cite: The quarter was reported successitiously.
words.etym: success + -itious, on fictitious, repetitious, surreptitious. An ear-word — -itious is inherited and no longer productive.
words.note: The nearest neighbour by sound is also the nearest by sense: fictitious.

words.def: Performing thought without conducting any — the held pause, the stroked chin, the hmm that precedes no consideration.
words.cite: He received the objection ponderatiously and answered it unchanged.
words.etym: ponder + -atious.
words.note: The weakest entry here, and one of mine. Built to replace ponderingciously, on a suffix described as freely productive when it is not — -atious is licensed by an -ation noun beneath it (ostentation, flirtation, vexation, disputation) and ponderation is archaic. It reached a sense ponderingly already covered. Three faults, all mine, on a word substituted for someone else's. Kept as a record of the reasoning, not as a recommendation.

words.pos: verb, present participle — from to flamingle
words.def: Mingling with the plumage on: attending an opening for the standing-about rather than the art — conspicuously present, decorative, one-legged, doing very little, and doing it beautifully.
words.cite: “How was the vernissage?” — “I was flamingling.”
words.etym: flamingo (Portuguese flamengo, ultimately Provençal flamenc, 'flame-coloured') + mingle (frequentative of Middle English mengen, 'to mix'). The two words are welded at /mɪŋɡ/, a string both of them already own.
words.note: This is the rarest join in the collection: the seam costs nothing. flamingo is fla-MING-o, mingle is MING-le, and the shared /mɪŋɡ/ carries primary stress in both. The founding rule here is that stress may travel one syllable and never two — flamingling makes it travel zero. Nothing is bent to fit, which is why it lands as though it were always a word. It also rebrackets flamingo into fla- + mingo, and that false seam hands back a full verb: to flamingle, flamingled, flamingling. Compare the eight seams below — this one parses.

image.caption: The word in the wild, August 2026. Poster by Venus of Artizen.

sightings.where: Poster by Venus of Artizen, gallery-opening photograph
sightings.what: Set as a two-line exchange over a vernissage scene: “HOW WAS THE VERNISSAGE?” / “I WAS FLAMINGLING.”

words.def: The clothing stratum on the bedroom floor, used as storage.
words.etym: floor + wardrobe. Wardrobe is Old French warderobe — guard-robe, a place to guard robes — so there is no morpheme -drobe. Ward, warden and guard are the same word, French having turned the Germanic w- into g-.
words.note: Already in dictionaries. A false seam that made it all the way in, which is the thesis of this project with an existence proof attached.

words.def: Fictions that make themselves real; an idea that, once circulating, functions causally to bring about the conditions it describes.
words.cite: I am the Director of Reality.
words.etym: Coined by the CCRU (Cybernetic Culture Research Unit, Warwick, 1990s). Superstitio is super + stare, 'to stand over' — there is no morpheme -stition. The seam was sliced wrong, the fragment reused, and the prefix swapped. Adverb: hyperstitiously, with a t.
words.note: Self-demonstrating at maximum depth: a word about fictions becoming real by circulating, which became real by circulating, formed by the mechanism it names. It also names what the founding image was doing — PlanetaryCouncil.org, an authority existing because someone typed it.

sightings.what: Title card reading HYPERSTICIOUSLY over the CCRU definition.

words.def: Institutional planning at ministry scale.
words.etym: Borrowed from French planification / Spanish planificación. English took the noun without the verb — we have planification but barely planify.
words.note: Planning has a planner in it; planification has no doer-slot at all, which is the feature. The -ification pattern this collection kept reaching for is fully alive one language over.

words.def: Audacity of a kind that inverts the frame — the offender claiming the victim's standing.
words.cite: Travelling internationally with an active arrest warrant to a city that does not welcome you.
words.etym: Yiddish, from Hebrew ḥuṣpāh.
words.note: Its canonical illustration — the man who murders his parents then pleads for mercy as an orphan — is exactly the structure two entries here went hunting for. Tu quoque and DARVO are the technical siblings; this is the ordinary-English one.

seams.truth: -ify + -ation; the i belongs to the stem side of the join
a -y noun + -ful + -ly; that i is the noun's own mutated y
needs a -ce or -ice stem (malice, caprice, grace, space)
delicious is Latin deliciosus; there is no -licious
wardrobe is warderobe, a guard-robe; there is no -drobe
superstitio is super + stare; there is no -stition

rules.body: Each suffix names a destination. They are alternate roads, not successive rungs — -ification plus -ously gains syllables without gaining density. The legal exit from -ification is -ationally.
Loophole, success, compost, remix, hack, war worked. Intertwine, reprogram, unhappen, prevent, expand are round trips, because -ify's only job is making a verb out of something that is not one.

rules.rule: Stress travels one syllable, never two
rules.body: dis·CLAIM·er becomes dis·clai·MER·cious·ly and holds. BRAIN·fart and le·GIT·i·mate cannot reach. Monosyllabic bases can never fail this test.
Secondary stress keeps a long tail from collapsing. WORD·smith·ing·ly survives four syllables; VIC·to·ri·ful cannot.

rules.rule: Clip the base to fix the meter
rules.body: Long word, early stress, suffix that pulls right? Shorten the base and the stress comes to meet the suffix instead of failing to reach it. legitimate → legit.

rules.rule: Libfixes want short, neutral bases outside their home field
rules.body: One or two syllables; the suffix supplies the judgment, so an already-evaluative base is redundant; and the field the fragment came from is saturated.

rules.rule: The suffix must carry the meaning
rules.body: Not just the part of speech. -licious encodes appetite, -ification encodes process. Neither encodes inversion — that is prefix territory.
Nothing derives further from them. Inflection, conversion and compounding still work.

rules.rule: Check whether the rules already built it
rules.body: Say it aloud. If it sounds merely unfamiliar rather than invented, it is not a coinage — it is English you had not happened to use. Ponderously, infographically, unhingedly, ponderingly, litigious and victoriously each killed a candidate.
Three accidents paid: mercy inside the founding word, Middle English -tioun from a slipped u, and a three-hundred-year-old split between flour and flower.

These rules describe what English currently does. They are weather reports, not permits. Three of eight false seams here are in dictionaries, and nothing distinguishes them from the other five except that enough people repeated them.
